newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says S.African energy deals to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says S.African energy deals to go ahead.

text.p: State-run utility Taiwan Power Company said on Thursday the change in Taiwan's diplomatic ties with South Africa would not affect the company's coal and uranium purchases from Pretoria.
"Whether we have diplomatic ties with the country (from which we purchase energy), has no absolute impact," Taiwan Power president Hsi Shih-chi told reporters.
South African President Nelson Mandela told reporters in Johannesburg on Wednesday that Pretoria would switch diplomatic ties from Taipei to Beijing by the end of 1997.
South Africa is the biggest of just 30 states that recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China rather than the communist People's Republic on the mainland.

Taiwan has reached a total of 4.7 million tonnes worth of coal supply contracts with South Africa this year and is close to finalising a 10-year contract to buy 300,000 pounds of uranium annually from South Africa, a Taiwan Power official said.
The uranium supply is expected to start in early 1997, the official said by telephone.
As all Taiwan Power's purchasing contracts follow international regulations and business practices, neither party to the deal can cancel a contract before it expires, he said.
Taiwan and China have been separated since a civil war ended in 1949.
China sees Taiwan as a rebel Chinese province not entitled to foreign ties while Taiwan insists its 21 million people have a right not to be excluded from international activities.
